subject: Canary cutover and temporary SLO derating request for bursty batch traffic
messages:
From: Mei Chen <mei.chen@kartelis.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Production cutover window + SLO question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're gearing up for a phased cutover of our inference pipelines to Redwood in mid-October. Before we lock dates with our infra team, two asks from our side: 1) can we run a small canary with 10% of traffic to validate tail latency under our hourly batch spikes, and 2) if we see transient p95 violations during the canary (expected during the hourly fan-out), can we agree to a temporary, timeboxed derating of the p95 target while we tune batching and routing?

Our current internal SLO is p50=70ms / p95=260ms for inline requests; batch-spike bursts push tail higher for ~15-20 minutes per hour. We want to avoid a full production SLA update but need a documented exception path for the cutover.

Best,
Mei
Director, Platform Engineering
Kartelis Inc.

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Mei Chen <mei.chen@kartelis.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production cutover window + SLO question

Hi Mei —

Really appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can run a phased canary and we have an established exception playbook for timeboxed SLO derating tied to canary validation and tuning. To be explicit, we recommend:

- Canary phase (10% traffic): 48–72 hours, daytime-only, with active monitoring.
- Measurement horizon: rolling 1-hour windows for p50/p95 during the canary but with a 24-hour aggregate evidence check for roll decisions.
- Temporary derating: allow p95 to relax to 350ms for defined 2-hour remediation windows (only if spike evidence shows sustained resource saturation), automatically revert after remediation or after 72 hours unless mutually extended.
- Rollback criteria: if error rates > 0.5% or p95 above 500ms for more than 30 minutes, revert canary to previous routing.

I'll attach a short runbook with the exact telemetry checks and escalation contacts. Can we sync Thurs to align the calendar? I'll loop in Marissa from Solutions for the SLA paperwork.

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kartelis-canary-runbook-v1.pdf (10 pages; runbook and telemetry queries)

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production cutover window + SLO question

Agree with the proposed guardrails. A couple of tweaks from legal/op policy that we'll need in the mutual action plan:

- Define exact measurement window used for contract reporting vs. canary telemetry. For contract purposes we use a 30-day rolling window; the canary will use the short windows you outline but any exception must not alter the baseline contract definition in the SLA.
- Record of evidence: customer-signed CSV export of canary telemetry (we will request a snapshot) + our internal tracing spans (obfuscated PII).
- Credit mechanics: if a production cutover exceeds the temporary derating window by >48 hours, crediting will be prorated.

I'll draft an addendum that clarifies measurement horizon and credit triggers. Ben — can you confirm the automation for the rollback alarm (Jira INF-7892) and ownership?

Lauren
Director, Customer Success

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production cutover window + SLO question

Confirmed — INF-7892 is the runbook automation ticket. Short summary of automation behavior:

- Canary health probe aggregates p50/p95 and error-rate every 60s.
- If p95 > 500ms for 30 continuous minutes OR error-rate > 0.5% for 15 continuous minutes, we flip routing to 0% (automatic rollback) and create a PagerDuty incident to oncall.
- If we detect short 10–20 minute p95 spikes (350–500ms) but no error increase, we mark an alert for ops and continue the canary; this is where the temporary derating (to p95=350ms) applies for planned tuning windows.

I've attached a sample CSV from our internal replay of a burst window so Kartelis can see the shape.

Attachment: burst-evidence-sample.csv
